email.description:
Unique email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be verified before posting or commenting.

This field is required for registration and must match the format of the email field in the discussion_board_citizens table.

Must be a valid email address that follows RFC 5322 standards. The system will verify uniqueness in the discussion_board_citizens table during registration process.

This field serves as the user's primary identifier for authentication and communication purposes.

password.description:
Plain text password for authentication. The system will hash this password using a secure algorithm (e.g., bcrypt) and compare it against the stored password_hash in the discussion_board_citizens table. Must meet security requirements (minimum length, complexity) as defined by the system policy.

The password must be provided in plain text format as this is the input field for registration. The backend system will immediately hash this value using a secure algorithm (bcrypt) and store the hash in the password_hash field of the discussion_board_citizens table.

For security: Must be at least 8 characters long and contain a mix of upper/lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters as defined by the system policy.

This field is mandatory and must be included in every registration request. Never transmit or store the password in plain text beyond this request context.

IDiscussionBoardCitizen.ICreate.description:
Request body containing the credentials required to register a new citizen account in the discussion_board_citizens table.

This schema defines exactly which fields the client must provide to create a new citizen account. It directly maps to the discussion_board_citizens database table, including only the fields that the client can provide during registration: email and password.

The email field must be unique across all records in the discussion_board_citizens table and must follow standard email formatting rules. The password field must meet the system's security requirements (minimum length, complexity) and will be hashed before storage.

Important: This schema does not include system-managed fields like id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, or email_verified as these are automatically handled by the system. The email_verified field is always initialized to false during registration and must be set to true through a separate email verification process.

This schema ensures minimal attack surface by only allowing the two necessary fields for registration, preventing injection attacks or unauthorized field manipulation.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated citizen user.

This corresponds directly to the id field in the discussion_board_citizens table, which is a UUID generated by the system upon account creation.

This identifier is included in the JWT token payload and is used to identify the user in all subsequent API requests. The system matches this ID against the discussion_board_citizens table to validate user ownership and permissions.

Format: UUID v4 as defined by RFC 4122 with hexadecimal representation (32 characters, 8-4-4-4-12 pattern).

IDiscussionBoardCitizen.IAuthorized.description:
Response containing authentication tokens and user information for the authenticated citizen user.

This schema defines the complete structure of the response returned after successful citizen authentication (login or registration). It follows the pattern I{PascalPrefixName}{ActorName}.IAuthorized where PascalPrefixName is 'DiscussionBoard' and ActorName is 'Citizen', as required by the system conventions.

The schema contains two critical fields:
1. id: The unique identifier of the authenticated citizen, referenced from the discussion_board_citizens.id field
2. token: A structured object containing all required authentication tokens

The token field is an object that references the IAuthorizationToken schema, which contains:
- access token (JWT with 30-minute expiration)
- refresh token (JWT with 7-day expiration)
- expiration timestamps (expired_at, refreshable_until)

This structure ensures standardized authentication across the application. The token is issued and validated by the system's secure authentication mechanism, using the citizen's data from the discussion_board_citizens table to populate the JWT claims.

After successful authentication, the user's role ('citizen') is embedded in the JWT payload, which determines their access permissions in the system. The email_verified status is not included in the response as it's not needed for authentication - the system enforces this at the endpoint level instead.

IDiscussionBoardCitizen.IRequest.description: Request body containing authentication credentials for a citizen user. Includes the email address and password required to authenticate against the discussion_board_citizens table. The email field is used to locate the user record, and the password is validated against the stored password_hash. This schema directly maps to the fields in the discussion_board_citizens Prisma model: email (unique identifier) and password_hash (hashed value). The schema requires both email (String, not nullable) and password (String) fields for authentication.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ICreate.description: Request body containing the credentials required to register a new moderator account. This object defines the data needed to create a new moderator account in the system. The email field must be a valid, unique email address that will serve as the authentication identifier. The password must meet security policy requirements and will be hashed by the backend before storage in the discussion_board_moderators table. This schema directly maps to the fields in the discussion_board_moderators Prisma model: email (unique identifier, not nullable) and password_hash (hashed value, not nullable). The email_verified field is not included in this schema because it is automatically initialized to false during registration and must be set to true through a separate email verification process.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated moderator, taken from the JWT payload.

This field contains the UUID that uniquely identifies the moderator in the system, corresponding to the id field in the discussion_board_moderators table.

The id is included in the JWT token payload during authentication and provides a direct reference to the moderator's account record in the database. This allows the system to validate the moderator's identity and permissions on every request without requiring additional database queries.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness across distributed systems and cannot be easily guessed or enumerated, providing security against enumeration attacks. All moderator-related operations on the platform use this identifier to establish account ownership and authorization context.

This field is essential for maintaining stateless authentication while providing unambiguous identification of the moderator making each API request.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized.description:
Response body contains the authentication tokens and moderator account information following successful authentication.

This schema defines the structure of the authorization response for a successfully authenticated moderator user. The object contains two essential fields:

1. id: A UUID that uniquely identifies the moderator in the system, taken directly from the JWT token payload and corresponding to the id field in the discussion_board_moderators table.

2. token: A reference to the IAuthorizationToken schema which includes:
   - access: The JWT access token for authenticated requests (30-minute expiration)
   - refresh: The refresh token for obtaining new access tokens (7-day expiration)
   - expired_at: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when the access token expires
   - refreshable_until: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when the refresh token expires

The IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized response is generated exclusively during the login process (/auth/moderator/login) and refresh process (/auth/moderator/refresh). It provides the minimal necessary information for clients to maintain authenticated sessions without exposing sensitive user data or system internals.

This schema directly corresponds to the discussion_board_moderators Prisma model, ensuring that the token structure references the user's unique identifier and role as stored in the database. The implementation follows the system's authentication requirements where moderators must authenticate before performing any moderation actions, and the token structure aligns securely with the JWT-based authentication system.

The x-autobe-prisma-schema field is included to establish a direct link to the Prisma model, ensuring traceability between the API schema and the underlying database structure. This link is critical for automated system components to validate consistency between the data model and API contracts.

Client applications must store the access and refresh tokens securely (e.g., in HTTP-only cookies or secure storage) and include the access token in the Authorization header for subsequent requests as "Bearer {token}". The refresh token must be protected and transmitted only to the refresh endpoint to maintain session security.

Note: The moderator's email, role, and other attributes are encoded within the JWT token itself and are not included in this response body to minimize exposure. This design follows the principle of least disclosure for secure authentication responses.

This schema type strictly adheres to the business requirements for moderator authentication as defined in 01-user-actors.md (Authentication Requirements) and ensures accurate modeling of the data flow from discussion_board_moderators to the authentication system.

message.description:
Success confirmation message indicating that the moderator registration was successfully initiated. The system has created a new moderator account in the discussion_board_moderators table with email_verified set to false. An email verification message has been sent to the provided email address, and the moderator must verify their email before performing any moderation actions. This message confirms the registration process started successfully but does not indicate the account is fully active yet.

The message content is standardized and localized based on the user's locale settings to ensure clear communication to the moderator user. This response is returned immediately after registration processing completes but before email verification is completed.

This message plays a critical role in setting user expectations: the moderator must understand that their account is not yet active and cannot be used until they complete the email verification workflow. This prevents confusion and support issues that would arise if users believed they could immediately access moderation features after registration.

The system synchronizes this message with the registration workflow, ensuring it matches the content sent in the verification email while providing immediate feedback during the registration process.

There are no additional fields included in this response as the objective is to provide minimal, clear, and unambiguous confirmation that the registration process has started correctly. All sensitive information (email, hashed password, UUID) is intentionally omitted for privacy and security reasons.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorWelcome.description:
Response data returned after successful moderator account registration. This confirms the creation of a new moderator record in the discussion_board_moderators table with email_verified set to false.

The system has initiated the email verification process to ensure the moderator's email address is valid before granting moderation privileges. The moderator must complete email verification before being able to log in and perform moderation tasks.

This message is returned immediately after the registration process completes successfully. It does not confirm that the moderator can access the system yet — authentication is blocked until email_verified becomes true through the separate email verification workflow.

This represents the lightweight success response following registration, which attempts to preserve state in the discussion_board_moderators table while providing feedback to the user. It specifically indicates success of the registration operation while acknowledging the necessary subsequent step (email verification).

The message content is generated by the system using a standardized template for registration confirmations, and this string is returned in the response. The message is localized based on the user's locale settings but maintains a consistent format.

The schema does not include the moderator_id, email, created_at, or other fields from the discussion_board_moderators table, intentionally omitting sensitive information to minimize exposure during registration responses while ensuring the user is aware of the required next step.

The x-autobe-prisma-schema field is included to establish a direct link to the Prisma model, ensuring traceability between the API schema and the underlying database structure. This link is critical for automated system components to validate consistency between the data model and API contracts.

email.description: Unique email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be verified before moderating content.

password.description: Password for authentication. Never stored in plain text. Required for login functionality. Password will be hashed by the backend and stored in the password_hash field.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking (OPTIONAL - server can extract, but client may provide for SSR). This field is included because this is a self-login operation where the actor is establishing their own session.

This field is a critical component for establishing the initial session context in the system. When a moderator logs in from a client device, the IP address associated with that request is recorded in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table. This information aids in security audits and helps detect account compromise patterns such as logins from unusual geographic locations. The system can extract this value from the HTTP request headers, but allowing the client to send it ensures more precise IP tracking in distributed or reverse-proxy environments.

href.description:
Connection URL (current page URL) - MANDATORY. This field is included because this is a self-login operation where the actor is establishing their own session.

This field records the exact page URL from which the moderator initiated the login process. This information is captured in the href property of the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table and is essential for user journey analysis and security logging. It helps track the entry points into the system and identify potential phishing scripts or malicious redirects that lead to login pages. For example, if the href is a suspicious domain not part of the legitimate application, it could indicate an attempt to harvest credentials. This field is mandatory for every login attempt and must be provided by the client as part of the authentication flow.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL) - MANDATORY. This field is included because this is a self-login operation where the actor is establishing their own session.

This field records the previous page URL from which the moderator navigated to the login page. This information is stored in the referrer property of the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table and is vital for security intelligence. It helps distinguish between legitimate logins (e.g., from the application's main page) and suspicious login attempts originating from third-party websites or malware. Helps prevent credential stuffing attacks and identify compromised referral sources. This field must always be provided by the client during login as a mandatory part of the session establishment.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ILogin.description:
Request body containing the moderator's email and password to authenticate and generate access tokens.

This schema defines the data required for moderator authentication. The email must exactly match an existing record in the discussion_board_moderators table and must have email_verified set to true. The password will be verified against the stored password_hash.

This operation is a self-login (authorizationActor: "moderator"), meaning the authenticated actor is themselves establishing their session. Therefore, session context fields MUST be included:
- ip: Client IP address (optional - server can extract from request)
- href: Current page URL (mandatory)
- referrer: Previous page URL (mandatory)

These session fields are written to the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table upon successful authentication. They are not authentication fields but rather connection metadata for audit and security purposes.

No owner, creator, or update fields are included because the system automatically associates the session with the authenticated moderator through JWT validation.

CRITICAL BUSINESS CONTEXT RESTRICTION: These fields (ip, href, referrer) are NOT used for authentication validation (which is handled by email/password). They are session tracking fields written to the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table during successful authentication, functioning as audit trails for every moderator session initiation.

refresh_token.description:
The valid refresh token used to obtain a new access token. This token was issued during the initial authentication (/auth/moderator/login) and must be valid and not expired.

This refresh token must be a JWT that is currently active and unrevoked. The system validates the refresh token against the token store and ensures that the associated moderator account referenced in the token payload exists and is not soft-deleted (id must correspond to a discussion_board_moderators record where deleted_at is null). Additionally, the refresh token must be linked to an active entry in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table, indicating that the original session has not been terminated. This function will fail if any of these conditions are not met.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRefresh.description:
Request body containing the valid refresh token to obtain a new access token.

This schema defines the required parameter to renew an expired access token. The refresh token must be valid and not expired, and the moderator account it authenticates must be active in the system (no soft delete). This operation is governed by business logic that requires the underlying moderator record to exist and be active (deleted_at is null in discussion_board_moderators). The refresh token must originate from a previous successful login and must not have been revoked via the system's token infrastructure. A valid refresh token always corresponds to a single active session in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table. This operation will only proceed if the associated moderator account record exists, has not been deleted, and represents a currently active authentication context.

updated_count.description: The number of configuration settings that were successfully updated. This value indicates how many of the provided configuration objects were matched with existing keys and modified in the database.

IDiscussionBoardConfigUpdateResponse.description: A confirmation object indicating the number of configuration settings successfully updated. This response is returned after successfully processing the batch update request to the discussion_board_configs table.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the configuration record.

key.description: Unique identifier for the configuration parameter. Examples: "max_file_size_per_post_mb", "allowed_image_types", "min_post_title_length".

value.description: String representation of the configuration value. Can be JSON-encoded for complex values (e.g., array of string types).

description.description: Human-readable explanation of what this configuration controls and its intended purpose.

category.description: Grouping for related configuration settings. Examples: "media", "content", "moderation", "session".

created_at.description: Timestamp when this configuration was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this configuration was last modified.

IDiscussionBoardConfig.description:
The configuration setting with its key and value as stored in the discussion_board_configs table.

System-wide configuration settings for the discussion board. Contains key-value pairs defining behavioral limits and policies that govern posting, commenting, file uploads, moderation actions, and report handling. Managed by administrators through external tools, not by end users.

IDiscussionBoardConfig.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing system configuration setting.

This schema defines the structure of the request payload when updating a configuration parameter via the PUT /discussionBoard/moderator/system/config/{key} endpoint.

The IUpdate type is an update variant of the main IDiscussionBoardConfig schema, representing the specific set of fields that can be modified by an administrative user. This update schema is intentionally partial - it includes only the properties that are permitted to be changed during an update operation.

This schema permits modifications to three specific fields:
- value: The new value for the configuration setting, transmitted as a string with appropriate encoding for complex types
- description: An updated human-readable description explaining the purpose and intent of the configuration
- category: A new organizational grouping for the configuration setting

Important notes on usage:
- The key identifier is specified in the URL path parameter, not in the request body
- The id field is not included here because configuration updates are performed by key, not id
- The created_at and updated_at fields are server-managed and automatically updated by the system when changes are made

This update schema ensures that only permitted fields can be modified, preventing accidental or intentional changes to critical system-managed fields such as ids and timestamps. The value field must be formatted according to the specific configuration parameter's requirements (simple string, JSON-encoded array, or JSON-encoded object). The description and category fields allow administrators to maintain accurate documentation and organization of configuration settings.

The schema is designed specifically for use with the update system configuration operation and is validated against the discussion_board_configs table in the Prisma database schema.

### Business Context

This schema represents an update operation for the discussion_board_configs table which stores system-wide configuration parameters that govern critical system behaviors:
- File upload limits (max_file_size_per_post_mb)
- Allowed file types (allowed_image_types)
- Content length requirements (min_post_title_length, max_comment_length)
- Session management parameters (session_timeout_minutes)
- Moderation policy settings (moderation_reported_minutes)

The key parameter in the URL path identifies the specific configuration setting to update, and the payload contains the new value, updated description, and optional new category for reorganization.

The system enforces strict validation on each configuration type:
- For numeric values (like file size limits), the string representation must parse as a valid integer
- For boolean flags, the string must be exactly "true" or "false"
- For array values (like allowed image types), the string must be valid JSON formatted as an array of strings

The configuration system provides the flexibility to change system behavior without code deployments, enabling rapid iteration based on user feedback and platform needs. However, these changes directly impact all users, so they require explicit moderator approval and are subject to full audit trail.

This schema should be used only for the update operation where a specific configuration key is identified in the URL path. It is not intended for creating new configurations or bulk updates.

This schema structure ensures that:
- Only necessary fields are accepted in the request
- Client cannot manipulate immutable fields like id, created_at, updated_at
- All changes are strictly controlled and auditable
- The API remains flexible to accommodate complex configuration types

Security consideration: The key is validated against the discussion_board_configs table to prevent injection attacks on configuration parameters. Only approved configuration keys can be modified here.

IDiscussionBoardCitizen.IRegisterRespons.description:
A success response confirming the registration request has been received and the verification email has been sent. The response contains the citizen ID and confirms that activation is pending email verification.

### Business Context

This response schema represents the system's confirmation to a citizen who has successfully initiated account registration on the discussion board platform. It follows the two-step registration process outlined in the requirements:

1. The user provides an email address and password via the IDiscussionBoardCitizen.ICreate request
2. The system creates a record in the discussion_board_citizens table with email_verified set to false
3. The system sends a verification email to the provided address
4. The system returns this IRegisterResponse to signal successful registration

This response is deliberately minimal to prevent exposing sensitive information about the registration process. It does not include the user's password hash, creation timestamp, or other internal metadata that could potentially aid attackers.

The schema contains only two fields:
- id: The unique UUID assigned by the system to the new citizen record
- email_verified: A boolean indicating the verification status (false, as per business requirements)

All other fields from the discussion_board_citizens table (email, password_hash, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are intentionally excluded from this response for security reasons. This follows the principle of least exposure - only providing the information necessary for the client to proceed with the registration workflow.

The client's next step is to instruct the user to check their email for the verification link. In some implementations, the client may auto-navigate the user to a "verification pending" page on the website. The response does not include tokens or session identifiers because no session has been created yet - the user must complete email verification and then log in via the authentication endpoint.

This approach enhances security by ensuring that:
- User credentials are never exposed in response
- Account creation cannot be abused through automated account enumeration
- Email verification is mandatory before any account activity can occur

The id field in this response allows the client to retrieve additional user information after the verification process is complete, but this ID should not be exposed publicly as it could be used to track users across different platforms.

Note: While the discussion_board_citizens table contains several additional fields, they are intentionally omitted from this response to reduce attack surface and maintain user privacy.

IDiscussionBoardCitizenLoginRequest.description:
Authentication credentials for citizen login

This schema represents the request body for citizen login authentication.

CRITICAL: Must contain exactly two fields: email and password.
Only these fields are accepted from the client.

The system performs password verification by comparing the provided plain-text
password with the hashed password stored in the discussion_board_citizens table.

The password field MUST be sent as plain text (not hashed), as the backend
handles the hashing during verification.

The email field MUST be a valid email format.

No other fields are permitted in this request.

THIS IS A DIRECT MAP TO THE AUTHENTICATION PROCESS DEFINED IN THE REQUIREMENTS.

Discussed in: 01-user-actors.md (Authentication Requirements)
Discussed in: 04-error-handling.md (Authentication Failures)

Ensure the field names match exactly what is required by the backend: 'email' and 'password'.

DO NOT use field names like 'emailAddress', 'user_email', 'password_hash', or 'hashed_password'.
DO NOT include field names like 'session_id', 'ip', 'referer', 'citizen_id', or 'role'.

This schema is for citizen authentication ONLY. Do not use it for moderator login.

Required fields: 
- email  
- password

Optional fields: 
- none

Field Validations:
- email: Must be a valid email format (RFC 5322) 
- password: Must be a non-empty string of at least 8 characters

Background:
This request is processed by the system during the login procedure. The backend validates:
1. The email exists in the discussion_board_citizens table
2. The password hash stored in the table matches the provided password
3. The citizen's email_verified flag is true

If any condition fails, the system returns a user-facing error message and denies authentication.

This schema MUST NOT be used to store or transmit hashed passwords. The system expects the plain-text password.

Related Test Case:
- Successful login with valid email and password
- Failed login with invalid email
- Failed login with incorrect password
- Failed login with unverified email
- Failed login with empty email field
- Failed login with empty password field

Security:
- Must be transmitted over HTTPS only
- Must not be cached
- Must be deleted from client memory after successful authentication

The system will issue a JWT access token upon successful authentication using this data.

Examples:
{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "password": "SecurePassword123!"
}

{
  "email": "invalid.email",
  "password": ""
}

{
  "email": "",
  "password": "password123"
}

Used by: POST /discussionBoard/auth/citizen/login

Derived from: 01-user-actors.md, 02-functional-requirements.md, 04-error-handling.md
related to discussion_board_citizens model

CRITICAL: Follow exact field names and structure. Do not modify.
DO NOT use any other fields, even if they seem 'logical' or 'required'. The schema has been designed to minimize attack surface and is non-negotiable.

IDiscussionBoardCitizenLoginResponse.description: Response containing authentication tokens and user information for the authenticated citizen user. Following the required pattern, this includes the access and refresh tokens. The schema for this response references the citizen email and role information directly from the discussion_board_citizens table and matches the pattern I{PascalPrefixName}{ActorName}.IAuthorized where PascalPrefixName is 'DiscussionBoard' and ActorName is 'Citizen'.

IDiscussionBoardCitizenRefreshResponse.description:
Newly issued JWT access token with 30-minute expiration for citizen user authentication. This token must be included in Authorization header for subsequent API requests. Format: JWT with HS256 signing, contains citizen id, role, and expiration time.

This token is a cryptographically signed JSON Web Token with the following claims:
- sub: citizen UUID
- role: "citizen"
- exp: expiration timestamp (30 minutes from issuance)
- iat: issued-at timestamp

The token is transmitted in the Authorization header using the Bearer scheme (e.g., 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...'). It does not contain sensitive data but enables stateless authentication for protected endpoints. The token must be refreshed before expiration using the refresh endpoint to maintain session continuity.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRequest.description:
Request body containing the moderator's email and password to authenticate and generate access tokens.

This schema defines the data required for moderator authentication. The email must exactly match an existing record in the discussion_board_moderators table and must have email_verified set to true. The password will be verified against the stored password_hash.

This operation is a self-login (authorizationActor: "moderator"), meaning the authenticated actor is themselves establishing their session. Therefore, session context fields MUST be included:
- ip: Client IP address (optional - server can extract from request)
- href: Current page URL (mandatory)
- referrer: Previous page URL (mandatory)

These session fields are written to the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table upon successful authentication. They are not authentication fields but rather connection metadata for audit and security purposes.

No owner, creator, or update fields are included because the system automatically associates the session with the authenticated moderator through JWT validation.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Unique identifier for the moderator session record.

discussion_board_moderator_id.description: References the moderator user who owns this session. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

href.description: URL where the user accessed the system during this session.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating the source of this session (e.g., which page linked to the login).

created_at.description: Timestamp when this session was created.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when this session expired or was invalidated. Nullable since active sessions have no expiration.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorSession.description:
Session tracking table for moderator users. Each record represents one active or expired authentication session for a moderator. Follows exact mandatory schema for actor session tables with no additional fields. Managed exclusively through the authentication system, not directly by users.

@namespace Actors
@author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe

This schema represents the session tracking record for authenticated moderators. The system creates a new session record when a moderator successfully authenticates via the /discussionBoard/auth/moderator/login endpoint, capturing essential connection metadata (IP address, referrer, href) and linking it to the assigned moderator through discussion_board_moderator_id.

The created_at field records the moment authentication was granted, while the expired_at field indicates when the session token expired (typically 30 minutes after creation). When a moderator explicitly logs out or the system invalidates the session (for security reasons), the expired_at field is populated.

The updated_at field is automatically updated by the system whenever the session record is modified, such as during explicit logout, session restart, or administrative session termination. This provides a complete audit trail of changes to the session record.

The deleted_at field implements soft delete behavior for sessions that have been logically removed from the system (e.g., when a moderator account is disabled). This ensures audit compliance while preventing the session from being used for authentication.

This session data is crucial for security auditing, detecting suspicious activity patterns, and session-based rate limiting. The system logs and analyzes this data to identify potential security breaches, such as multiple sessions from different locations or sessions with suspicious header information.

refresh_token.description:
The valid refresh token used to obtain a new access token. This token was issued during the initial authentication (/auth/moderator/login) and must be valid and not expired.

Refresh tokens are long-lived (7-day) JSON Web Tokens (JWT) that contain the moderator's ID and role in the payload, signed by the system's secret key. When presented to the refresh endpoint, the system validates the token's signature and expiration, then generates a new access token with a 30-minute expiration.

This token must be stored securely on the client-side (e.g., in localStorage or a secure HTTP-only cookie) and transmitted only to the /discussionBoard/moderator/auth/moderator/refresh endpoint. Refresh tokens must never be included in API request headers alongside access tokens, nor should they be included in client-side logs.

The refresh token implements a security pattern where short-lived access tokens (30 minutes) are used for API calls, minimizing exposure risk, while long-lived refresh tokens (7 days) allow for seamless session persistence. The system maintains a record of used refresh tokens to prevent reuse and implement token rotation policies.

Security note: If the refresh token is compromised, the system will invalidate it and require the moderator to re-authenticate with credentials. This prevents token theft from persisting across multiple sessions.

IDiscussionBoardAuthRefreshRequest.description:
Request body containing the valid refresh token to obtain a new access token.

This schema represents the payload for the refresh token endpoint (/discussionBoard/moderator/auth/moderator/refresh). It is used exclusively by moderators and requires a valid refresh token that was issued during the initial login phase and has not yet expired.

The refresh token is a JWT that contains the moderator's ID and role, signed by the system's secret key. The refresh endpoint validates the signature and expiration of this token, then issues a new access token while keeping the same refresh token (unless token rotation policies apply).

This system implements a secure authentication pattern where access tokens have short expiration times (30 minutes) to minimize exposure in case of interception, while refresh tokens have longer lifetimes (7 days) to allow users to remain logged in without frequent re-authentication.

The refresh request does not authenticate the moderator by username and password, but by cryptographic verification of the refresh token. This design reduces the attack surface compared to repeated password-based authentication. The client must ensure the refresh token is stored securely and not exposed to malicious scripts.

The system enforces refresh token rotation, meaning a refresh token can only be used once. When a refresh token is used to obtain a new access token, the original refresh token is invalidated and a new one is issued with a 7-day expiration. This prevents token theft from enabling persistent access to the account.

IDiscussionBoardAuthRefreshResponse.description:
Returns a new access token (JWT) with a 30-minute expiration and a refreshed session context, containing the moderator's ID and role.

The access token is a JSON Web Token signed by the system's secret key with expiration set to 30 minutes from issuance. The payload includes the following claims: id (moderator UUID), role ("moderator"), iat (issued at timestamp), and exp (expiration timestamp).

This token must be included in the Authorization header of subsequent requests to protected endpoints as a Bearer token.

Example: "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."

IDiscussionBoardPost.description: The complete created post entity including its system-generated identifier, creation timestamp, and author reference.

IDiscussionBoardPost.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new discussion board post.

This schema defines the minimum set of fields required from the client to create a new post. It excludes system-generated fields like id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, status, citizen_id, moderator_id as these are controlled by the backend.

Only user-provided content fields are accepted in this request body, following the principle that clients submit only data they directly control. This ensures security and attribute ownership integrity by preventing client-side manipulation of system-managed fields.

Fields included:
- title: required, minimum 5 characters
- body: required, minimum 10 characters

Excluded fields are:
- id (auto-generated)
- created_at, updated_at, deleted_at (server-managed timestamps)
- status (determined by system rules)
- citizen_id (set from authenticated user)
- moderator_id (set only by moderator actions)

This schema strictly adheres to business rules: post creation requires a non-empty title and body, and all other fields are automatically populated during server-side processing.

This schema is used exclusively in the POST /discussionBoard/citizen/posts and POST /discussionBoard/moderator/posts endpoints.

Security note: All values in this schema are validated by the backend against the requirements (minimum length, presence) before being persisted.

title.description: Updated title for the discussion board post. Must be at least 5 characters long according to business rules.

body.description: Updated body content for the discussion board post. Must be at least 10 characters long according to business rules.

IDiscussionBoardPost.IUpdate.description: Fields to update for the discussion board post. Only title and body can be modified. Note that editing is restricted by time and permissions based on actor role.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for filtering, sorting, and pagination of comments.

This type defines the request schema for searching and retrieving paginated lists of comments.

The fields correspond to filtering criteria, sort options, and pagination controls required for
efficient retrieval of comment data from the discussion_board_comments table.

- `page` and `limit` control pagination.
- `status` filters comments by their current state (active, deleted_by_author, deleted_by_moderator).
- `author_type` filters comments by the type of the author (citizen, moderator).
- `search` performs full-text search on the comment content using PostgreSQL trigram matching.
- `order_by` specifies sorting direction and field (created_at descending is default).

Key constraints:
- page: must be >= 1
- limit: must be >= 1 and <= 100 (enforced by server)
- status: must be one of the valid status values
- author_type: must be one of the valid actor types
- search: can contain arbitrary text for full-text search
- order_by: must be one of the allowed sort fields

The search functionality only applies to the `content` column and uses database-specific trigram
indexes for performance. The query does not search in author names or post content.

Example: A citizen wants to find all their own comments containing the word "help".
They would set:
- author_type: "citizen"
- search: "help"
- page: 1
- limit: 20
- order_by: "created_at:desc"

This schema is used by the /discussionBoard/comments endpoint for search operations.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Unique identifier for the comment in the discussion_board_comments table. Automatically generated by the system upon creation and used as the primary reference for all interactions with this comment.

This UUID ensures global uniqueness and prevents sequential ID guessing attacks. It serves as the primary key for all database operations and API references to this comment.

discussion_board_post_id.description:
The post this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_posts.id}.

This foreign key establishes the hierarchical relationship between the comment and its parent post. The comment's visibility and context are entirely dependent on the parent post's status. When the associated post is removed, this comment is effectively orphaned from the public discussion.

The system enforces referential integrity to ensure every comment is associated with exactly one valid post, and this field cannot be modified after creation.

author_id.description:
The ID of the user who created this comment. Can be either a citizen or moderator. Use author_type to determine which table to reference. {@link discussion_board_citizens.id} if author_type is "citizen", {@link discussion_board_moderators.id} if author_type is "moderator".

This field stores the unique identifier of the entity that authored the comment. It enables the system to accurately attribute the comment to the correct user and enforce access controls based on ownership and role permissions. This is a critical field for implementing business rules around editing and deletion.

The value is populated automatically by the system from the authenticated user's JWT token during creation and cannot be modified by clients.

oneOf.description:
The type of user who authored this comment. Must be either "citizen" or "moderator". This discriminates which subtype table contains the actor-specific details.

This discriminator field is essential for the polymorphic ownership pattern used in the system. It determines whether the author is a citizen or a moderator, which affects the permission rules for editing, deleting, and moderating this comment. This field ensures referential integrity without requiring nullable foreign keys in the main table.

Business rules:
- Only citizens with verified email can create comments
- Moderators can create comments on any post
- Both citizen and moderator authors can be moderated

See also: discussion_board_citizens, discussion_board_moderators

content.description:
The content of the comment. Must be between 1 and 1,000 characters as per requirements. Never null due to minimum character constraint.

This property stores the actual textual content of the comment as provided by the user. The business rules mandate a minimum of 1 character and a maximum of 1,000 characters to prevent empty comments and excessively long content that could impact performance or usability. This field is the primary content of the comment and is displayed directly to other users.

Character limits are enforced to:
- Maintain conversation flow and readability
- Prevent spam and automated posting
- Ensure consistent UI rendering across all devices
- Support efficient search indexing

Note: The actual display may truncate content for visual presentation if longer than 300 characters, but the full content is preserved. The system enforces these constraints at creation and update time.

oneOf.description:
The current status of the comment. Values: "active" (normal state), "deleted_by_moderator" (removed by moderator with [Deleted by moderator] message), "deleted_by_author" (removed by original author with [Deleted by author] message). Used to control visibility and moderation actions.

This status field implements the system's soft delete policy for comments. An 'active' status means the comment is visible and accessible.

Soft delete principles:
- Maintains audit trail of all content changes
- Preserves rollback capability
- Prevents data loss while ensuring compliance
- Supports transparent content moderation
- Enables content recovery under specific circumstances

All comments start with 'active' status upon creation.

'deleted_by_moderator' indicates a moderator has removed the comment but the record is preserved for audit purposes, with content replaced by '[Deleted by moderator]'. created_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was originally created. Required for chronological display and audit trail. Always present.

This field captures the exact moment the comment was first submitted to the system. It is immutable and is used to display comments in chronological order (oldest first) as required by the business rules. This timestamp is critical for maintaining the integrity of the conversation history and for auditing purposes to track when content was added.

The system ensures:
- A UTC ISO-8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ)
- Automatic server-side generation at time of creation
- No client-supplied timestamps allowed
- Enforced by database triggers and application validation

This field enables:
- Correct chronological display of comments
- Implementation of 24-hour editing window policy
- Compliance with historical record requirements
- Generation of time-based analytics

See also: deleted_at, updated_at

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was last updated (e.g., edited). Required for tracking modifications and display of [Edited] marker.

This field is updated whenever the comment content is modified by an authorized actor (the original author within 24 hours or any moderator at any time). It provides a mechanism to detect changes after initial creation and to display an '[Edited]' marker on the comment to indicate that its content has been modified since its original submission. This supports transparency in content changes.

The system ensures:
- Automatic server-side update on successful content modification
- Value is unchanged for the lifetime of inactive comments
- No modification allowed after 24 hours for citizens
- Only moderators can update this field regardless of time
- Always reflects the most recent content change

This field is critical for maintaining user trust in content integrity and ensuring that small corrections are visible while preventing major revisions.

See also: created_at, deleted_at

deleted_at.description:

This field records the exact time when a comment was marked for removal either by the original author or a moderator. When the status changes to 'deleted_by_moderator' or 'deleted_by_author', this field is populated with the current timestamp. If the comment remains active, this field is null. This provides a precise audit trail of when deletions occurred, separate from the status field which indicates the current state.

The system ensures:
- Automatic population when status changes to deletion state
- No user-modifiable value
- Server-side timestamp generation
- Comparison with created_at to determine deletion latency

This field is essential for:
- Identifying immediate vs delayed deletions
- Informing moderation reporting
- Enabling recovery operations in edge cases
- Generating deletion statistics

See also: status, updated_at

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
User comments on discussion board posts. Comments are primary entities requiring independent management, search, and filtering. Each comment is associated with a specific post and authored by either a citizen or moderator. Comments have a character limit of 1,000 and display in chronological order. When deleted by a moderator or author, the content is replaced with a system message while preserving authorship and timestamp for audit purposes. Uses polymorphic ownership pattern with author_type field to distinguish between citizen and moderator authors.

@namespace Comments
@author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe

For a complete understanding, relate this entity to the following:
- discussion_board_posts: Each comment must reference exactly one post
- discussion_board_citizens: Author of comment when author_type = 'citizen'
- discussion_board_moderators: Author of comment when author_type = 'moderator'
- discussion_board_reports: Any comment may be reported via this association
- discussion_board_moderation_actions: Administrative actions taken on this comment

This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern by using author_type (citizen/moderator) with author_id, avoiding nullable foreign keys while maintaining referential integrity.

The soft delete mechanism (status and deleted_at fields) ensures compliance with audit requirements while maintaining a clean user experience.

This entity is at the core of community engagement on the platform. Every comment contributes to the conversation history and represents user voice in the digital space. The architecture prioritizes:
- Flexibility to support multiple content types
- Transparency in moderation
- Preservation of historical context
- Scalable performance for high-volume comments

discussion_board_post_id.description:
The post this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_posts.id}.

This foreign key links the comment to its parent post and is required for creation. The system validates that this post exists and is in 'active' status before allowing the comment to be created. This field is essential for establishing the comment's context within the discussion structure.

The system enforces referential integrity by validating against the discussion_board_posts table. Only posts with status 'active' can accept new comments. The value is provided by the client and must be a valid UUID from the discussion_board_posts entity.

content.description:
The content of the comment. Must be between 1 and 1,000 characters as per requirements. Never null due to minimum character constraint.

This property must be provided by the client during comment creation. The system validates that the content is not empty and does not exceed 1,000 characters. This is the only user-provided field in the creation request, and it represents the actual text of the comment as intended by the author.

Content validation rules:
- Minimum 1 character (trim whitespace)
- Maximum 1,000 characters (before any processing)
- No HTML/JS injection allowed (server-side sanitization)
- No prohibited words (based on moderation configuration)

This field directly maps to the content column in the discussion_board_comments table and is the only user-controllable value submitted in this request.

The client must ensure the content meets these constraints before submission to avoid validation errors. The system will reject any request that violates these constraints with an appropriate HTTP 400 error response.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate.description:
This request body schema defines the parameters required to create a new comment in the discussion_board_comments table. It includes the minimum required fields for initial comment creation into the system. Notably, this schema excludes fields that are auto-generated or derived from the authentication context, describing only the information the client must submit.

Key points:
- id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, and status are generated by the system upon creation and are not provided by the client.
- author_id and author_type are determined from the JWT authentication token and are not submitted by the client.
- The reason for this structure is security: Values like author_id and author_type must not be provided by the client as they are critical to access control. Instead, the system validates the authenticated user's role and identity from the token.
- This design implements the principle that user identity must come from verified authentication tokens, never from request bodies.

This schema is used for both citizen and moderator comment creation endpoints, as the only difference between them is the authentication context, not the request structure.

Client-side constraints:
- Must include discussion_board_post_id (valid UUID)
- Must include content of length 1-1000 characters
- Must send authentication token
- Must not send any fields beyond those listed here

Server-side validation will ensure:
- The post referenced by discussion_board_post_id exists and has status 'active'
- The authenticated user has a verified status (email_verified = true)
- The content length is between 1 and 1000 characters
- The user's role (citizen or moderator) is valid per the authentication token

Note: The status value 'active' is assigned by the system automatically upon creation per business requirements.

This schema directly implements the business requirement: 'THE citizen SHALL be able to submit a comment with a minimum of 1 character and a maximum of 1,000 characters.'

Security imperative: This schema design prevents privilege escalation attacks where a malicious client might attempt to impersonate another user by setting author_id to a different value. The system's authentication middleware enforces that the JWT token's user ID is used as author_id, completely ignoring any client-provided values.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate.description:
Updated content of the comment; a string with 1 to 1,000 characters.

This is the only field that can be modified in a comment update operation. The business rules permit critical edits to be made only under specific conditions:
- Citizens may update their own comments within 24 hours of creation
- Moderators may update any comment at any time

When an update is performed, the system validates that:
- The new content is not empty
- The new content is 1,000 characters or fewer
- The authenticated user has the rights to update this comment (either author within time limit or moderator)

The content is replaced in its entirety with the new value provided in this field. Other fields like author_id, author_type, created_at, and status must not be modified by this operation as they represent immutable attributes of the comment's history.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.description: File attachments associated with posts on the discussion board. Each attachment represents a single file uploaded by a citizen, with metadata for file type, size, and moderation status. Attachments are managed independently by moderators who can view, download, and remove them, replacing links with [Attachment removed by moderator]. This table stores the physical file reference and metadata while supporting audit trails through soft deletion. Associated with discussion_board_posts via foreign key.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination parameters for retrieving attachments.

This structure defines the query parameters for searching and paginating attachment records. It supports filtering by status, file type, creation date ranges, file size ranges, and full-text search on filenames.

This schema is used exclusively for search/list operations (GET/PATCH requests) and does not modify data. It does not reference any Prisma model directly as it represents query parameters, not table columns.

This schema has been corrected to require at least one filter (status, filetype, or search) to prevent unbounded queries on the discussion_board_attachments table. Page and limit now have explicit validation bounds per system policy.

All numeric fields now have appropriate minimum constraints matching production rules. Descriptions have been augmented to reference the discussion_board_attachments model.

query.description:
Search term or keyword to match against post title and content.

This field represents the user's text query for finding relevant posts:
- Case-insensitive matching is performed
- Full-text search is enabled using PostgreSQL's trigram index
- Matches can occur in either title or body fields
- Supports partial word matches for improved user experience
- Allows word stemming for better relevance

The search feature returns posts with the highest relevance score based on matching words in both title and content.

This is the only required field for search operations - clients must specify what content they're looking for.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results (1-based index).

The system implements traditional offset pagination with the following constraints:
- Must be a positive integer starting from 1
- Allows navigation through sorted search results
- Each page contains exactly 20 results
- Maximum page limit is enforced to prevent performance issues on large datasets
- Current implementation allows up to 100 pages

For example, page=1 returns first 20 results, page=2 returns results 21-40, etc.

This parameter ensures clients can efficiently retrieve large result sets without overwhelming the system.

Note: There is no cursor-based pagination - this uses simple offset-based pagination for implementation simplicity.

limit.description:
Number of results to return per page.

This parameter controls the size of each page of results:
- Must be between 1 and 100
- Normally fixed at 20 per business requirement
- Maximum allows for very specific cases where clients need to fetch more than 20
- Combined with 'page' parameter to compute offset (page - 1) * limit

The system uses this value to limit result set size for performance optimization.

Note: While 20 is the standard page size, the API accepts up to 100 to accommodate special use cases.

IDiscussionBoardPost.IRequest.description:

This schema defines the query string parameters used for searching and retrieving a list of discussion posts filtered by keywords. It follows the HTTP GET request pattern with URL-encoded parameters.

Security and Query Sanitization:
- This schema contains no user IDs or authentication data
- All parameters are essentially full-text search keywords with pagination
- Pages are strictly validated (positive integer)
- Limits are capped to prevent overly large queries (max 100)
- No SQL injection risks - these parameters are sanitized server-side

Behavior:
- Only posts with status 'active' are returned (query parameter doesn't override this rule)
- Inactive, deleted, or pending posts are never included in results
- Results are always ordered by created_at DESC (newest first)
- Only title and body fields are searchable - no filtering by author, comment count, etc.
- There is no support for sorting by relevance or date asc

This DTO does not map to any database table - it is purely a request object for search operations. The data it contains is not stored in the database.

The response is paginated using this information with fixed page size of 20.

IDiscussionBoardReport.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a discussion board report for display in moderation queues.

This schema provides an essential, structured summary of a report for moderator review. Main entity capturing the audit event of a moderation action performed by a moderator.

This is the central record that stores the action type, reason, timestamp, and discriminator for the moderated entity. Each moderation event (edit or delete) is a discrete business transaction.

References to specific moderated entities (posts, comments, or attachments) are handled through subsidiary tables to ensure referential integrity and compliance with 3NF normalization. This is NOT a standalone table; it must be joined with one of the three *_of_* subsidiary tables to determine what exactly was moderated. The moderator_id is not included in this DTO because it is automatically retrieved from the authenticated moderator's JWT token during authorization, not provided by the client. This follows the security principle that the actor's identity must come from verified authentication context, not request bodies.

This schema enforces the business rule that every moderation action must have an action_type ('edit' or 'delete') and optionally includes a reason. The system validates that the requesting user has moderator privileges before accepting the request.

IDiscussionBoardPost.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a discussion board post intended for list views and search results.

This schema defines a reduced data model for displaying a post as part of a collection, such as the main feed or search results page. It is optimized for performance and client-side rendering speed.

Structurally:
- Uses only essential fields for identification and display
- Excludes full body content to prevent large JSON payloads
- Calculates and includes aggregate counts for comments and attachments
- Excludes system-level and audit fields

Comparison with full post:
- Full post (IDiscussionBoardPost): 8 fields, includes body content
- Summary post (IDiscussionBoardPost.ISummary): 5 fields, excludes body content

Benefits:
- 3-5x smaller payloads on list views with 20+ posts
- Faster parsing and rendering on client side
- Reduced bandwidth consumption
- Improved server response times

Overview of included fields:
1. id: required for client-side post linking and detail navigation
2. title: primary content indicator for user engagement decisions
3. created_at: allows chronological sorting and recency assessment
4. comments_count: leveraged for gauging community engagement
5. attachments_count: indicates presence of supplemental resources

Restricted fields:
- body: excluded to prevent display of large text in lists
- citizen_id: excluded for privacy (only exposed via ID reference)
- moderator_id: excluded as not relevant for summary views
- status: excluded as summary views only contain active posts
- updated_at: omitted as summary views indicate recency via created_at
- deleted_at: excluded as summary views only show active, non-deleted posts

This schema ensures consistency in listing interfaces across the application.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description:

This summary schema is designed for high-performance listing pages where only essential comment information is needed to allow users to make informed decisions about which comments to read in detail.

Compared to the full detail view, this summary eliminates large text fields and nested content to reduce payload size and improve response times.

The schema prioritizes:
